elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 expressly states that Customer shall pay Vendor “no liquidated damages” and removes the original fifteen-percent weekly liquidated-damages charge.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 expressly states that Customer shall pay Vendor “no penalty, and no amount in the nature of either.”

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer is solely an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no liquidated amount at all, so the condition that Customer owes a liquidated amount is demonstrably absent. This is more protective than limiting such amounts to an early-termination fee.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the condition requiring application of the three-month cap is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative language eliminates the original weekly liquidated-damages charge and expressly negates both liquidated damages and penalties, satisfying the preferred position. The fallback is also satisfied because no liquidated amount or early-termination fee is imposed. The revision preserves unrelated payment obligations and remedies, but it is not strictly minimal because “and no amount in the nature of either” goes beyond the language needed to negate liquidated damages and penalties. The retained conditional and phrase “for each week the invoice remains unpaid” also make the resulting sentence awkward.
